newsitem.title: PERU: Peru July inflation seen at 0.7 pct - Apoyo.
newsitem.headline: Peru July inflation seen at 0.7 pct - Apoyo.

text.p: Peruvian consumer prices rose 0.7 percent in July, and 4.9 percent in the first half of 1997, leading private research firm Apoyo SA estimated Monday.
That would compare with 1.4 percent consumer price inflation in July last year and 7.8 percent cumulative inflation in the first seven months of 1996, according to government figures.
July's inflation was led by rises in food and domestic service prices, Apoyo said in a statement.
The government is due to announce the official July inflation figure Friday.
According to the government, Peruvian consumer prices rose 1.1 percent in June and 4.1 percent in the first half of the year.

Consumer prices in Peru rose 11.8 percent in 1996, after a 10.2 percent rise in 1995. The government estimates accumulated consumer inflation will be nine percent this year and will drop to "the level of industrialized countries" by 2000.
